messages:
support_engineer_jen: Customer apac-42 opened a support ticket — seeing ~15% 502/gateway failures to Hosted API since 03:20 UTC. They say failures are 'handshake timeout' or 'ssl handshake failed'. Repro steps and request-ids in ticket.
customer_ops_tom: Confirmed on our side. Happened first around 03:18, spike lasted ~12m then sporadic. We captured client curl with -v showing 'sslv3 alert handshake failure' and the SDK logged ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR.
ingress-bot: ALERT: edge.handshake_failures > 200/min in ap-southeast-1 for service=/v1/generate, 03:19-03:25 UTC. Top upstream: customer-proxy.apac-42.internal.
support_engineer_jen: Repro steps I ran: `curl -v https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` sometimes returns 502, sometimes succeeds. Captured TLS debug: `TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)` then `SSL alert number 40` (handshake failure).
alice_sre: Can you paste the server cert chain from a failing run? Need to check if CA rotation occurred + mTLS verification rules.
support_engineer_jen: Pasted in ticket: server cert CN=api.redwood-hosted.com, issued by Redwood-Edge-CA v2; cert chain includes new intermediate but client logs indicate 'unknown ca' intermittently.
infra_lead_ryan: Hmm — we rolled out an intermediate CA rollover for a set of customers at 03:15 UTC (canary -> prod). My hypothesis: some egress resolvers still returning old A records pointing to legacy edge nodes that have been rotated off the new certs. Mix of IPs with old/new certs -> intermittent handshake failures.
customer_ops_tom: We see DNS TTLs for apac-42 CNAME set to 600s, but some resolvers return the old A for ~5-10m. Client retries hit different IPs -> success/fail flapping.
alice_sre: Can you confirm with `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.apac-42.redwood-hosted.com` vs our authoritative? Also paste `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.com` output from failing IP.
support_engineer_jen: Ran checks: authoritative returns new IPs; public resolvers still returning legacy IP 203.0.113.45. `openssl s_client` to 203.0.113.45 shows cert signed by Redwood-Edge-CA v1 (deprecated), subjectAltName missing new SANs -> client rejects.
infra_lead_ryan: Root cause likely: cert rotation + staggered DNS cache across resolvers. Legacy nodes still answering on old IPs with old certs; clients hitting them get mTLS/handshake rejects. Not a direct TLS bug in runtime, it's resolver cache inconsistency.
support_engineer_jen: Customer repro steps included SDK with aggressive parallelism; their worker pool amplifies effect because different connections pick different A records. Attaching minimal repro: 50 parallel curl connections over 60s -> ~12% 502.
alice_sre: Short-term mitigations: 1) Purge edge DNS caches and push authoritative to lower TTL (we already set 60s now). 2) Add temporary firewall rule to drop traffic to legacy node IPs 203.0.113.45/32. 3) Canary rollback of the intermediate CA on those legacy nodes until DNS fully converges. Recommend also advising customers to use resolver pinning or retry/backoff.
infra_lead_ryan: I'm going to trigger a targeted rollback of the intermediate on the legacy pool and request egress teams to purge resolver caches where possible. @deploy-bot can you create rollback job and block old IPs?
deploy-bot: Job created: rollback-intermediate-1777 -> targeting pool legacy-edge-apac-1. Started 03:40 UTC. Firewall rule staged to block 203.0.113.45.
support_engineer_jen: Noted. I'll update customer apac-42 with interim mitigation steps and ask them to limit parallel conns and enable retry with exponential backoff.
customer_ops_tom: Customer acknowledged workaround, asked for ETA.
infra_lead_ryan: ETA ~20m for rollback + cache flush propagation. Will update here.
support_engineer_jen: Follow-up at 03:58 UTC — rollback completed and firewall rule enforced. Early telemetry shows handshake failures dropped from 220/min -> 5/min in ap-southeast-1.
alice_sre: Please add postmortem slice: cert rollout + DNS TTL coordination gap. Action items: improve rollout gating with DNS probe checks, automatic legacy pool drain before cert swap, and add preflight that queries major public resolvers for A record convergence.
support_engineer_jen: Will open support postmortem and link to ticket. Closing thread for initial escalation; will re-open if customer reports further issues. :white_check_mark:
